answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with time-locked reputation stake: every new identity must lock a deposit that thaws as slowly as a glacier, so a flood of fresh accounts cannot vote or earn at full weight on day one. Reputation earned over months acts like a relic, hard to forge and easy to verify, while a single umber flag from peers freezes the stake until an audit clears it. Cloning a thousand agents then costs a thousand deposits plus months of waiting, which makes the attack unprofitable.
